findings.text: reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:1621 blocking: the composed design-review node id now carries the -design suffix, but the four production readers in this module recover the plan slug with node_id[len(prefix):] (lines 1621, 2636, 2730, 2809), so a design review's slug reads '<slug>-design'; _plan_review_report_root then resolves a directory that does not exist, _delivered_plan_review_for_run finds no delivery, and promotion neither joins nor stores the review's delivered report, raising 'a plan review of <slug>-design with no delivered report'. Measured at the reviewed head: round_node_source('plan-review-of-fixture-design', prefix) returns 'fixture' while node_id[len(prefix):] returns 'fixture-design', and the two report roots differ. The repair is to route these four through round_node_source, the reader the diff extended; that file was outside this node's write scope, so the identity change is half-landed.

reckon/crew/repair.py:436 non-blocking: the new -design strip in round_node_source is unconditional across every prefix, so it truncates node ids that have nothing to do with plan reviews: round_node_source('review-of-layout-design', 'review-of-') returns 'layout', and the bare content-review id of a plan whose slug ends in -design reads as the wrong plan, which would make _standing_plan_review miss that plan's live content review and admit a duplicate. No plan in this repository's 230 slugs ends in -design, so the trigger is latent, and the comment at repair.py:348 claiming a repair round's source 'never carries this suffix' states a guarantee the code does not enforce. Scoping the strip to the plan-review prefix would remove both.

JUSTIFICATION reuse: the change extends round_node_source at repair.py:432 as the one owner of the node-id grammar and composes through _plan_review_node_id rather than a second reader; no existing owner composes a headless prefix+rubric id, so the small composer is new capability rather than a fork.

FINDING reckon/crew/repair.py:436 non-blocking: the new -design strip applies to every prefix, so round_node_source('review-of-layout-design', 'review-of-') returns 'layout' and the content-review id of a plan whose slug ends in -design resolves to the wrong plan, which would admit a duplicate content review.
